narratives.title: Super Intelligence coins
narratives.summary: On Sept. 29 Trump said AI would officially be renamed "Super Intelligence" (Fox News). On 2026-10-04 the official @WhiteHouse account posted an announcement of a "Super Intelligence Force (SIF)", and Watcher.Guru and an @wallstreetbets post reported Elon Musk saying SpaceXAI will be renamed SpaceXSI; a 2026-10-15 post reports that the task force is due to hold its first meeting (e1:4). Super Inu ($SI), launched Sept. 21, re-pitched itself around the term; other coins followed, including another SI on pump.fun, Super Intelligence Force (SIF), Superintelligence Owl, two SpaceXSI coins on StonkFun, SpaceX Inu ($SI on Flap), Act II: The SI Prophecy, and three BNB Chain coins on Flap named TeslaSI ("Tesla Super Intelligence", pool created 2026-10-11; a second whose Chinese metadata says it follows the SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI rename; and, since 2026-10-20, テスラSI, pool created 2026-10-19 02:34 UTC, whose Japanese metadata says Musk announced SpaceXAI becomes SpaceXSI and describes a 3% trade tax with 30% paid as on-chain dividends to holders). The Tetsuo Super Intelligence coin on pump.fun (TSI, Solana) joined on 2026-10-18 with a pool 4.6 hours old at discovery: traders' posts call TSI "another SI coin" and one says Elon Musk posted about it (e1:1), which is unverified. Its Clanker twin on Robinhood Chain left on 2026-10-20 after 24h pool volume of $277 and then $0. SPACEXSI and Ollie (pump.fun) left on 2026-10-17, and SIGF (pump.fun) and SuperHooks (Pons) on 2026-10-18, after their 24h pool volume stayed under $1,000. None is shown to be affiliated with the announcements. SpaceXSITeslaBoringaLink (SXSITBL, pump.fun) joined on 2026-10-19: its name combines SpaceXSI with Tesla and Boring, its pool was created on 2026-10-19 at 03:47 UTC, and nothing seen ties it to the announcements. Smaller coins named for SpaceXSI or TSI under the $100K market cap bar are not counted. 四 ("four", read as SI) on four.meme left on 2026-10-21 after its 24h pool volume stayed under $1,000. Measured: fourteen coins across all their pools.

story.notice: The White House SIF and SpaceXSI posts still date from 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-15 (e1:3; a post of 2026-10-15 says the new task force was reported to hold its first meeting that Thursday, not verified here), and the newest $SI and TSI posts (2026-10-18, e1:1) come from traders. si.gov (StonkFun) left on the under-$1,000 rule; SpaceX Super Intelligence (SpaceXSI, Flap, BNB Chain; pool created 2026-10-22 10:48 UTC) joined on its description.

narratives.title: Post-quantum coins
narratives.summary: Coins that market themselves on post-quantum cryptography and the "bunker mode" debate. On 2026-10-07 Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake posted a call for the industry to "calmly begin planning for 'bunker mode'", recommending a controlled mass migration of assets to fresh addresses whose public keys stay hidden behind a hash; coverage ties the call to AI-accelerated math breaking wallet cryptography. The same day Vitalik Buterin posted that he does not recommend scrambling to move funds today but that risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math, next to quantum, should be taken seriously, and The Block reported Europol urging the industry to prepare for quantum threats. pqc.market describes launching pump.fun coins with hash-based post-quantum attestations (WOTS one-time keys, Merkle identities); its own coin PQC and the coins QI (Quantum Inu), Tardigrade, Quantcum and BNKR (Bunker Coin) say in their metadata that they launched with its post-quantum proofs, BUNKER (Bunker Mode) describes vaults with separate hash-based authorization, and Qhost (QHOST, on Robinhood Chain) calls itself a quantum-resistant launchpad whose coins sit behind keys a quantum computer cannot break. All seven pools were created after the 2026-10-07 posts. None is shown to be affiliated with Drake, the Ethereum Foundation or Europol, and the coins' security claims are not verified. Measured: seven coins across all their pools.

narratives.title: Flying Tesla Roadster coins
narratives.summary: Coins named for the Tesla Roadster unveiling. Posts dated 2026-10-16 describe Tesla showing a next-generation Roadster with SpaceX cold-gas thrusters at SpaceX's Texas test site on the evening of 2026-10-15: it drove up a ramp, flipped in the air and landed, with a claimed 0-60 mph in 0.81 seconds and deliveries in 2028 (@niccruzpatane, @cb_doge); DEXTools quotes Tesla's "Real life, baby" caption and Elon Musk's reply "Turns out the future does have flying cars". Seven coins carry the name: two FTR contracts on Solana's pump.fun (Flying Tesla Roadster, and "Farting Tesla Roadster", whose metadata says "Everyone came for the movie"), a 特斯拉能飞 ("flying tesla roadster") coin on BNB Chain (Flap), a second Flying Tesla Roadster (FTR) on Flap, Starman (STARMAN, "the driver of the flying Tesla Roadster") Roadster (Flap), whose Chinese metadata refers to Musk and Tesla's new sports car and carries a QQ contact number, and, since 2026-10-19, Flying Tesla Dogester (DOGESTER, pump.fun), whose metadata says "Doge just learned to fly" (pool created 2026-10-18, after the unveiling). Posts of 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-19 announce FTR spot listings on KCEX, LBank and KuCoin Alpha (e1:3). The Meteora DBC FTR contracts left on 2026-10-17 and the Clanker 特斯拉能飞 on Robinhood Chain on 2026-10-18 after 24h pool volume under $1,000. The main pump.fun FTR says it pairs with $SPCX and $TSLA through OTC desks; its pool was created on 2026-10-15 at 02:08 UTC, before the unveiling, as was the Flap Roadster pool (04:28 UTC), while the other pools were created after it. An older FTR on StonkFun, created in August, predates the story and is not included, and a further pump.fun FTR is quarantined for an implausible market cap and extreme 24h move. These are traders' and the coins' own claims: no coin is shown to be affiliated with Tesla, SpaceX or Elon Musk, most are days old, and the story is a single event. Measured: seven coins across all their pools.

Papertrade's site (papertrade.xyz, e1:0) says "1000x leverage, 0 market impact, 100% user owned, fully onchain on hyperliquid". Posts of 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-20 say PAPER traded as a pre-launch perpetual on Hyperliquid through Paragon and that the market was halted and settled after Papertrade said PAPER would not be transferable (e1:4, one post, not verified here); the newest $PAPER post (2026-10-22 16:00 UTC, e1:4) is from a strategy account about the emission design. Paper coins copying Papertrade's tagline come from Clanker and change from day to day: a Paper contract on Robinhood Chain (pool created 2026-10-23 03:21 UTC) joined today, the Base contract from 2026-10-21 (0xd0814c...) stays, and the Base contract from 2026-10-20 left because its 24h pool volume stayed under $1,000 on two consecutive observations (membership stays open). Virtual Trade (VIRTUAL, pump.fun) describes itself as a perpetual trading protocol for memecoins with up to 1000x, and FloatSheets (FLOAT, Pons, Robinhood Chain) as a synthetic equity perps platform; both joined today on their descriptions (e2:7, e2:8). EmpireX (EMPIREX, Pons, Robinhood Chain) says it is a perpetual trading hub powered by Hyperliquid. Purps (PURPS, Meteora DBC) says it launches perp-backed tokens. Aloooong (pump.fun) calls itself the "First 10x PUMP long perpetual meme". These are the projects' and traders' own claims: revenue, leverage, payouts and affiliation among the coins are not verified. Measured: the coins named above across all their pools.

story.notice: Posts of 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-20 (e1:4) say PAPER traded as a pre-launch perpetual on Hyperliquid through Paragon, and one post (2026-10-20 12:12 UTC) says that perp lived 36 hours and was halted and settled at $0.0263 after about $15M of volume once Papertrade said PAPER would not be transferable (not verified here). The newest $PAPER post (2026-10-22 16:00 UTC, e1:4) is from a strategy account about PAPER's emission design, not from Papertrade. Papertrade's site (e1:0) still reads "1000x leverage, 0 market impact, 100% user owned, fully onchain on hyperliquid". A new Clanker Paper contract on Robinhood Chain (pool created 2026-10-23 03:21 UTC, copying Papertrade's tagline) joined today, with Virtual Trade (pump.fun) and FloatSheets (Pons, Robinhood Chain), whose descriptions say they are a perpetual trading protocol and a synthetic equity perps platform (e2:7, e2:8). The Base Paper contract that carried the volume on 2026-10-22 shows $59 today.
story.interpretation: Perpetual-futures venues are a real, dated theme, but the Paper coins are copy contracts that change within a day or two: each day a new Clanker contract takes the volume the previous one had. 24h volume to 04:00 UTC is $21.10M, down 63.6% on the preceding 24h window ($57.91M, when the Base copy ran); 94.7% is the new Robinhood Chain Paper ($19.97M, 1.9x its $10.5M market cap), Virtual Trade is 3.8% ($794K) and FloatSheets 1.4% ($303K, 4.2x its $72K market cap). Nothing seen links the Paper contracts to Papertrade. Treat the volume as young-pool trading.

narratives.summary: Coins from launchpads and projects that tie memecoins to tokenized stocks. STONK (StonkFun) says "Launch tokens / Backed by stocks", and @LaunchOnSF posted on 2026-10-12 that coins can be launched paired with $XPL on StonkFun (e1:8). XSTOK says it lets users launch and trade tokens paired with stocks; @xstokfun posted on 2026-10-16 that xstok is open and pairs a coin with any stock on Raydium or Meteora, and a 2026-10-17 trader post reports the XSTOK / NVDAX pair at a $190.9K market cap (e1:8). OTC says "Over-The-Counter Desks, earn stocks, pre-ipo, and yield". GTA VI (GTA6, StonkFun) says holders earn $TTWO stock by airdrop. A 2026-10-18 post says Flap's "memestock-3" coin is paired with a tokenized GameStop stock on BNB Chain (e1:9); it is not counted. These are the projects' and traders' own claims: payouts, stock holdings and volumes are not verified, and no affiliation among the coins was checked. The Robinhood Chain stock-token coins (BORRO, IRIDIUS) and the AI-stocks meme BUBBLE are not counted. Measured: four coins across all their pools.

narratives.title: French protest coins
narratives.summary: Coins named for the French protests of 2026-10-17. Le Monde and the BBC report that nationwide cost-of-living protests on 2026-10-17 turned to clashes, looting and arson in Paris and other cities (800,000 marchers by the organizers' count, 550,000 by the interior minister's; about 1,800 arrests), and that President Macron addressed the nation on 2026-10-18 (e3:1, e3:2). Three pump.fun coins on Solana carry the story: The French Doomsday (Doomsday), whose metadata reads "Avengers-level protests in France, live and unhinged", and two contracts named French Goku Hero (PIERRE), whose metadata is empty. Trader and scanner posts of 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19 call French Goku Hero a French internet figure from the riots and one relays a claim that he posted about a looted shop in Nice on 2026-10-17 (e2:1); a post of 2026-10-19 says his own coin is a different contract, so which PIERRE contract, if any, is the intended one is unclear (e2:1). All three pools were created on 2026-10-18, 8 to 14 hours before discovery, and most posts about the coins are call-group promotion. These are traders' and the coins' own claims: nothing seen links the coins to the people or events reported. Measured: three coins across all their pools.

narratives.title: GTA 6 Dacity Coin coins
narratives.summary: Coins named for Dacity Coin, an in-game meme coin that posts say appears in GTA 6 material. On 2026-10-11 the account @robtmb1 (RobTheMaster) posted that there is a meme coin in GTA 6 called "Dacity Coin" in a new leak (e4:0); the first Dacity Coin on pump.fun was created 35 seconds later (token created 2026-10-11 11:16 UTC, post at 11:15 UTC). A post of 2026-10-19 from the GTA 6 Intel account says DacityCoin appears on a stunt plane in GTA VI's launch trailer, a fictional crypto brand parodying real meme coins (e4:1). An automated claim check rated the claim "partly real" on 2026-10-18, saying the Dacity Coin name in GTA 6 material is real and widely reported but the leak timestamp and the leak's authenticity were not verified, and an earlier check on 2026-10-15 called it unclear (e4:0). Four coins carry the name: Dacity Coin (pump.fun, Solana; token created 2026-10-11), AudaCity (pump.fun; token created 2026-10-15 13:22 UTC), Dacity Coin (Pons, Robinhood Chain; created 2026-10-19 16:13 UTC) and GTAVI AudaCity (pump.fun; created 2026-10-20 04:04 UTC), whose metadata repeats the claim: "There's a meme coin in GTA 6 called \"Dacity Coin\" in the new leak." The other three have empty metadata, so their names carry the claim. Most posts about the coins are call-group promotion and listing-vote spam, and none of the coins is shown to be affiliated with Rockstar, Take-Two or the leak. These are traders' and the coins' own claims. Measured: four coins across all their pools.

story.notice: The newest post in the search (e1:6, 2026-10-21 10:14 UTC) still repeats that a meme coin called "Dacity Coin" appears in the GTA 6 leak and promotes the Dacity contract; a post of 2026-10-21 09:44 UTC says the Dacity coin is "sitting at 13m". Older posts (2026-10-11 to 2026-10-19) trace the claim to one streamer's post, and an automated claim check rated it "partly real" (name real and widely reported, leak authenticity not verified). No news outlet or official Rockstar or Take-Two page was fetched. GTAVI AudaCity ($0.38 of 24h volume on 2026-10-22) left on the under-$1,000 rule.
story.interpretation: The in-game reference is claimed by posts and not verified here, and the coins are copies named after it. 24h volume to 04:00 UTC is $5.67M, down 42.2% on the preceding 24h window ($9.81M) across 3 coins; the first Dacity Coin is 91.8% ($5.21M, 0.4x its $13.4M market cap) and DacityCoin 8.2% ($462K). Treat the volume as young-coin trading around a single story.

narratives.title: Pump.fun card-gacha coins
narratives.summary: Coins named for, or describing, Pump.fun's trading-card gacha with Collector Crypt. Posts of 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 say Pump.fun put Collector Crypt card packs (gacha) and a card marketplace into its app (e4:0): the earliest such posts in the sample are from 2026-10-19 19:04 to 19:13 UTC; a post from the CoinGecko account on 2026-10-20 (07:50 UTC) says $CARDS was up 19% that day following Pump.fun's integration of Collector Crypt's gacha, and a post of 2026-10-20 (04:59 UTC) says about $2M of gacha packs had been opened in the Pump.fun app since its launch the day before, about 20% of Collector Crypt's gacha spend that day. A recap post says the launch "spawned $COLLECTOOOR to $1m and pumped the $pokemon coin launched" (e3:1). Five coins on covered launchpads carry the theme: two coins named the collectooor (COLLECTOOOR, pump.fun; pools created 2026-10-19 18:59 UTC and 2026-10-20 02:52 UTC), two named Pokémon (pump.fun, pool created 2026-10-20 00:01 UTC; MeteoraDBC, pool created 2026-10-20 10:02 UTC) and filled.cards (FILLED, pump.fun; pool created 2026-10-02, well before the integration), whose metadata reads "Limit orders and trading terminal for Cards. Powered by @Collector_Crypt". Only FILLED has a description; the other four have empty metadata, so their names and the posts carry the link. None of the coins is shown to be affiliated with Pump.fun or Collector Crypt, and most posts about them are call-group promotion. Measured: five coins across all their pools.

narratives.title: Kimchi coins
narratives.summary: Coins named Kimchi, after the trader known on X as @kimchi1x. Posts of 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21 say Kimchi joined Pump.fun: a reply from his own account to @Pumpfun at 00:00 UTC on 2026-10-21 reads "let's work" (e3:0), and the Pump.fun Ecosystem account posted that he "BEAT his $40M Trump trade in 1 HOUR after joining Pumpfun" (e3:0). An account named kimchlsol posted at 04:20 UTC on 2026-10-21 that it is committing its entire position, 75% of the total supply of $KIMCHI, to a distribution for eligible community members (e2:1); another post disputes the wallet people link to him (e3:0). Trader posts name the Pump.fun contract CSocnz... (market cap about $33M in one post, e3:1), but that contract, a second Kimchi Coin contract and a third Aura Final Boss contract carry the quarantine flag for an extreme 24h move (pools about 6 to 7 hours old) and are not counted. Five other coins carry the name in their own metadata: a Kimchi (symbol Kimchi, "Aura Final Boss") on Clanker V4 on Robinhood Chain, a Kimchi on pump.fun whose description reads "official kimchi coin", Kimchi Boss (KIMCHIBOSS) and a coin named kimchi on pump.fun, all with pools created between 23:08 UTC on 2026-10-20 and 00:45 UTC on 2026-10-21, and an older Aura Final Boss (symbol Kimchi, pump.fun) whose description names @kimchi1x and which predates the story: its pool was created on 2026-07-27. A post of 2026-10-21 (e3:1) says that older contract pumped to about $7M in the last few days. These are traders' and the coins' own claims: no coin is shown to be affiliated with Kimchi, and several contracts call themselves official.

story.notice: Posts of 2026-10-23 (e1:2) say the trader Kimchi removed Pump.fun from his X bio: @lookonchain (05:34 UTC) writes that two days after the coin's launch he removed @Pumpfun from his bio, that Pump.fun's revenue fell 16% from $1.61M to $1.35M over those two days, and that he "may have received" 1.35B $PUMP ($6.25M) in marketing; @Velvet_Capital (05:43 UTC) says the token fell 50% on the news (all unverified here). DEXTools retold the 2026-10-20 story on 2026-10-21 (Pump.fun posted about @kimchi1x and he replied "let's work"). Two coins joined today: a Clanker copy on Base created at 02:50 UTC (Aura Final Boss, symbol Kimchi) and project kimchi on pump.fun (10 hours old); the Robinhood Chain Kimchi left on the under-$1,000 rule. The contract the posts name (CSocnz..., pump.fun) is not counted (a deferred candidate, see the report).
story.interpretation: The story is still being posted, and today's volume sits in new copies of the coin. 24h volume to 04:00 UTC is $61.12M against $2.26M in the preceding window across 6 coins (30-day volume of the same coins $22.70M, which does not yet include the Base copy because its pool was created after the last complete UTC day); 84.2% is the Base Kimchi ($51.44M, 4.9x its $10.5M market cap) and 15.5% project kimchi ($9.45M, 35x its $268K market cap, which carries the volume caveat). The contract the posts name is not counted, so this narrative still measures lookalikes. No coin is shown to be affiliated with Kimchi; treat the volume as young-coin trading around one trader's name.

narratives.title: PHP2Shell coins
narratives.summary: Coins named for PHP2Shell, the name security posts give to two critical PHP core flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 9.2 each, unauthenticated remote code execution). Posts of 2026-10-21 (e1:8) say the PHP project would ship an emergency security release at 14:00 UTC that day; at 15:35 UTC Rapid7 posted that the PHP project had announced security releases for the two flaws and that exploitation in the wild was expected, and a security-news account linked a Register article headlined that PHP developers published the fix and warned site owners to pull unpatched servers offline (e1:8). A post of 2026-10-22 summarising an AWS report says exploitation was seen on 2026-10-17, four days before disclosure (e1:8; not verified here). Four pump.fun coins carry the story in their own metadata: PHP-UP-2026 (PHP), whose description reads "They dropped an exploit that allows you to drain money from anyone." and whose pool was created at 05:14 UTC on 2026-10-21, before the 14:00 UTC release; two coins named PHP2SHELL (pools created at 04:21 UTC and 21:30 UTC on 2026-10-21, empty descriptions); and Saviour of the Internet (SURY), created at 00:05 UTC on 2026-10-22, whose description says its fees go to Ondrej Sury's GitHub (@oerdj) and credits him with rushing out emergency PHP patches. Posts of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 (e2:0) say a Debian PHP package maintainer named Sury published patched packages, including backports to end-of-life PHP versions, and one repeats the claim that the coin's fees go to his GitHub. The fee routing and any payout are the coin's own claim and are not verified, and no coin is shown to be affiliated with the PHP project, the researchers who found the flaws or Sury.

story.notice: Posts of 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23 (e1:7, e1:8) say the PHP project released emergency security fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on 2026-10-21 (Rapid7, 15:35 UTC: exploitation in the wild is expected). A security firm's post of 2026-10-22 14:58 UTC (@Huntio, e1:7) says attackers are staging the leaked exploit and that "no one has landed it", and a post of 2026-10-22 05:14 UTC says exploitation attempts and automated scanners are hitting its servers. A post of 2026-10-23 05:47 UTC (e1:8) is a crypto exchange's notice that it does not use PHP. The four coins are unchanged; none is shown to be affiliated with the PHP project, the researchers or Sury.
story.interpretation: The vulnerability story is real and current, but the coins are copies launched around it and their trading has cooled. 24h volume to 04:00 UTC is $6.90M, down 46.0% on the preceding 24h window ($12.77M) across 4 coins; PHP-UP-2026 is 58.5% ($4.03M, 13x its $311K market cap), Saviour of the Internet 32.6% ($2.25M, 115x its $19.5K market cap) and the two PHP2SHELL coins 9.0% together, and the volume caveat is shown for all four. Treat the volume as young-coin trading around a news event.

presentation.description: Tax-token launchpad on Arc. Each launch mints its whole supply into a single-sided Uniswap v4 position held by a locker with no withdrawal path, so there is no bonding curve and no migration — the token trades in a real v4 pool from block one, and a per-launch hook charges a buy/sell tax on every swap.

provenance.scope: all activity captured by mapped DefiLlama adapter

methodology.Fees: The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.
methodology.Revenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.

presentation.description: Rapid Launch is a token-deployment and trading toolkit that lets users deploy tokens across major launchpads and manage bundled buys, wallets, and automated trading workflows.

feeModel.note: Deployment toolkit spanning multiple launchpads. Fees and graduation mechanics belong to the selected underlying launchpad.

provenance.scope: all activity captured by mapped DefiLlama adapter
provenance.supportedChainCoverage: Nine chains advertised on homepage; seven fit current ChainId, Stable and Ink retained separately

methodology.Fees: SOL fees paid by users for Rapid Launch token deployment and trading tools.
methodology.Revenue: 86% of collector fees, kept by Rapid Launch after the 14% referral split.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: 86% of collector fees, kept by Rapid Launch after the 14% referral split.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: 14% of collector fees, distributed to referral recipients.

launchpads.supplySideDefinition: 14% of collector fees, distributed to referral recipients.

launchpads.name: BaseStonk

presentation.name: BaseStonk
presentation.description: BaseStonk is a launchpad where every token opens in a Uniswap v4 pool priced in a tokenized stock, ETF, major or stablecoin, with a BaseStonk hook on the pool

feeModel.note: Tokens open directly in Uniswap v4 pools. Hook and creator fee settings vary by launch.

provenance.scope: all activity captured by mapped DefiLlama adapter
provenance.supportedChainCoverage: verified subset; not an exhaustive live network availability guarantee

methodology.Fees: The tax BaseStonk's Uniswap v4 hook takes on every swap in a launched token's pool, from the hook's FeeTaken event. Each launch sets its own buy and sell rate. A buy pays the tax in the launch token and a sell in the pair; token-denominated amounts are converted into the pair at the pool price the same transaction's Swap reports.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's cut of the tax plus what reaches BSTONK holders: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade to the treasury, any part of the creator's cut the payee list left unplaced and the hook swept to the treasury, and the share of the creator's cut paid to BSTONK's dividend distributor, to the BSTONK basket vault, or burnt as BSTONK.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury's take: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade, plus unplaced creator fees swept to it.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Value to BSTONK holders, paid by the hook in the transaction the fee was taken: BSTONK's own pool pays its creator cut to BSTONK's dividend distributor and burns half of it, and launches carry the BSTONK basket vault as a payee; the vault pays BSTONK holders in rounds. Base only - BSTONK lives on Base.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator's cut of the tax less what the treasury swept and what reached BSTONK holders: the creator's wallets, the launch token's own holders through its dividend distributor, the burn of the launch token and the hook-owned liquidity wedge, as each launch configured them.
methodology.Volume: The pair side of every swap in a taxed pool, including the creator's dev buy at launch and excluding the hook's own buyback and liquidity swaps. Counted under Uniswap v4 as well.

launchpads.supplySideDefinition: The creator's cut of the tax less what the treasury swept and what reached BSTONK holders: the creator's wallets, the launch token's own holders through its dividend distributor, the burn of the launch token and the hook-owned liquidity wedge, as each launch configured them.

presentation.name: four.meme
presentation.description: Four.meme is a premier fair launch platform for meme coins on the BSC chain. Our platform is dedicated to empowering creators and communities to launch successful meme coin projects with ease.

provenance.scope: all activity captured by mapped DefiLlama adapter
provenance.supportedChainCoverage: verified subset; not an exhaustive live network availability guarantee

methodology.Fees: All fees paid by users for launching, trading tokens.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Fees retained by the four.meme protocol after rev-share distributions, the same as revenue.

launchpads.name: Foci

provenance.scope: all activity captured by mapped DefiLlama adapter
provenance.supportedChainCoverage: verified subset; not an exhaustive live network availability guarantee

methodology.Fees: All trading fees settled into FociFeeEscrow during the day (curve fees, creator tax, converted post-graduation hook fees, curve referral fees), plus hook referral fees claimed that day. Recognised when swept by the keeper, not when traded.
methodology.UserFees: Same as Fees: every fee is paid by traders on buys and sells.
methodology.Revenue: Protocol fee recipient's share plus the share paid to holder-reward distributors.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: Escrow credits to the protocol fee recipient (the protocol's frozen share of each launch's trading fee).
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Escrow credits to FociRewardsDistributor contracts — launches that elected to pay their creator share to token holders.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: Escrow credits to creators (their fee share and the creator tax) and to referrers, plus hook referral claims.

launchpads.supplySideDefinition: Escrow credits to creators (their fee share and the creator tax) and to referrers, plus hook referral claims.

excluded.stonkfun: Contains LaunchLab platform fees; post-migration component not separated
excluded.bonk.fun: Shares LaunchLab curve fees; post-migration component not separated
excluded.bags: Solana DBC overlap; Robinhood and post-migration components not separated
excluded.binance-alpha: Execution-route fees may overlap underlying venues; no component partition

feeSubtotal.scope: Sum of 14 non-overlapping mapped fee streams for the last complete UTC day. Omits 5 overlapping rows; some included adapters cover only one version. Not an all-roster total.

creatorEarnings.scope: DefiLlama supply-side revenue over the last 7 complete days, venues that define it; each venue's definition differs (creators, holders, referrers or traders).

indexed.scope: Codex beta provider-indexed counts for mapped launchpad names; rolling windows; omitted venues are unknown, not zero.

rolling7d.note: Narrative volume: collected coins counted once, hourly, to 2026-10-23T04:00:00Z. Fees: the 7 settled UTC days to 2026-10-23T00:00:00Z (daily data has no hourly split).

coverage.coverage: All activity captured by the mapped DefiLlama adapter; adapter scope differs per venue (registry venues[].scope). Use totalDataChart, never total24h.
Beta provider-indexed counts per named launchpad. Exact cutoffs, creation-event completeness and finality are not independently established. Rolling windows: never sum into calendar weeks.
All indexed pools of the token, aggregated by Codex (from mid-2025). Missing buckets are unknown, never zero, except whole buckets before the token's creation time (precreation-zero-provenance.json).
One row per token; the token is identified through pair.token0/token1 because Frames redacts response keys named token.
Ranked sweep with liquidity and volume floors: a sample of active tokens on covered launchpads, not a census.
Per requested token.
One page as rendered for the scraper. App shells, bot checks and geoblocks are not usable evidence.
Top-results convenience sample; no mention totals, no historical mindshare. Reposts of one claim are one claim.
Ranked board as the site orders it: a sample of currently active coins, not a market census.
Ranked home-page feed: a broader sample than trending, still not a census.
One coin; holder count is pump.fun's figure.

Positions held by pump.fun accounts, largest first (50 per page; limit=100 is rejected). Not the largest on-chain holders: on 2026-10-20 PIERRE listed 526 positions against 3,890 on-chain holders, top-10 share 10.6% against 25.2% on chain. Never all holders, never ownership history.
Most recent trades only (<=200 per call): a tape sample, not exhaustive history.
At most 1000 most recent buckets: depth = count x res. Historical depth must be confirmed per coin.
Matches ranked by USD market cap. Name matches are not identity: resolution always ends in an exact mint.
Top traders by profit on one coin: a profit-ranked sample, biased toward winners. Realized P&L here is source-reported, never a substitute for LAMBLE's reconstructed realized losses.

Events among FOMO users only. FOMO always adds its pinned manual post even when types= excludes it: classify after retrieval; a pinned post is never the newest trade. A third-party Frames probe note (2026-10-19) reports 4 items for limit=3, consistent with the pinned post being added on top of the requested page.
FOMO's curated lists; most-held reflects FOMO users' holdings only.
One token; top-10 holder share and buyer/seller counts are FOMO's figures. Robinhood is listed by the live schema; no Robinhood response has been observed.
